claims.statement: In a meta-analysis of placebo-controlled trials of medications for methamphetamine or amphetamine withdrawal searched to December 2020 (nine trials of six medications, about 240 participants, six trials at high risk of bias), no medication other than amineptine differed from placebo on any pooled outcome: discontinuation with any medication RR 0.70 (95% CI 0.40–1.23); with mirtazapine RR 0.96 (0.48–1.92); withdrawal-symptom scores SMD 0.17 (−0.43 to 0.77). Amineptine, tested in two small trials by one group, reduced discontinuation (RR 0.22, 0.07–0.72; very low certainty) but was withdrawn from the market in 1999 after reports of liver toxicity and non-medical use. Only one trial reported adverse events by arm.
claims.magnitude: Discontinuation, any medication RR 0.70 (0.40–1.23), 6 trials, 186 participants; mirtazapine 0.96 (0.48–1.92); modafinil 0.67 (0.22–2.03); amantadine 1.33 (0.34–5.24); amineptine 0.22 (0.07–0.72). Withdrawal symptoms SMD 0.17 (−0.43 to 0.77), 3 trials, 93 participants. Craving SMD 0.34 (−0.77 to 1.45), 2 trials, 48 participants.
